# Inphinit Framework Documentation

> Inphinit is a lightweight, high-performance PHP micro-framework designed to take advantage of native PHP functions and use a concise structure to process route callbacks, consuming minimal server resources.

## Introduction

- [Getting started](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/): Initial guide to installing Inphinit, creating a project and running your first application.
- [Structure](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/structure.html): Explains the directory and file organization of an Inphinit project and the role of each one.
- [API documentation](https://inphinit.github.io/api/2.1/): Complete reference of the classes, methods and functions of framework version 2.1.

## Web servers

- [Apache](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/apache.html): How to configure Apache (with `.htaccess` and URL rewriting) to run Inphinit applications.
- [Caddy & FrankenPHP](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/caddy-frankenphp.html): How to configure Caddy and FrankenPHP to serve an Inphinit application.
- [IIS](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/iis.html): How to configure IIS (with `web.config` and URL rewriting) to run Inphinit applications.
- [IIS Express](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/iis-express.html): How to run and test Inphinit applications on IIS Express in a development environment.
- [Lighttpd](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/lighttpd.html): How to configure Lighttpd to run Inphinit applications.
- [Nginx](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/web-servers/nginx.html): How to configure Nginx with PHP-FPM to run Inphinit applications.

## Routing

- [Routes](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/routing/): How to define routes, HTTP methods, parameters, patterns, filters and scopes.
- [Implicit routes](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/routing/implicit-routes.html): How to map routes automatically from controllers, without declaring them one by one.
- [Resource-oriented routes](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/routing/resource.html): How to create RESTful-style routes for listing, creating, editing and removing resources.

## Core features

- [Controllers](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/controllers.html): How to create and organize controllers to handle route requests.
- [Views](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/views.html): How to create and render views, including passing data to them.
- [Configurations](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/configurations.html): Lists the framework's configuration options and how to change them.
- [Debugging](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/debugging.html): Tools and options for debugging the application and diagnosing errors during development.
- [Maintenance](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/maintenance.html): How to put the application in maintenance mode and customize the response shown.
- [Error pages](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/error-pages.html): How to customize the pages displayed for HTTP errors such as 404 and 500.
- [Console commands](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/console-commands.html): How to create and run application console commands from the command line.
- [Task scheduling](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/task-scheduling.html): How to schedule periodic task execution without needing multiple cron entries.
- [Events](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/events.html): How to register and dispatch events to react to points in the application lifecycle.
- [Session](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/session.html): How to manage user sessions and store data between requests.
- [Checkup](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/checkup.html): How to verify that the PHP environment and installation meet the framework's requirements.

## HTTP

- [HTTP request](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/http/request.html): How to access request data: headers, parameters, body, uploaded files and cookies.
- [HTTP response](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/http/response.html): How to set headers, status codes and content of the response sent to the client.
- [Content negotiation](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/http/content-negotiation.html): How to choose the response format and language based on the `Accept` headers sent by the client.
- [Response codes](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/http/response-codes.html): Reference of HTTP status codes and how to use them in the framework.

## DOM (Document Object Model)

- [DOM, XML and HTML](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/dom/): Overview of how to manipulate XML and HTML documents using Inphinit's DOM classes.
- [CSS selectors in PHP](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/dom/css-selectors.html): How to use CSS selectors to query DOM elements, with conversion to XPath.
- [DOM with arrays](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/dom/dom-with-arrays.html): How to build XML and HTML documents from PHP arrays.
- [DOM errors](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/dom/errors.html): How to catch and handle errors and warnings raised when processing DOM documents.

## Utilities

- [Utilities](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/utilities/): Overview of the helper classes and functions provided by the framework.
- [URLs](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/utilities/url.html): How to generate, manipulate and validate application URLs.
- [Version](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/utilities/version.html): How to query and compare the framework and PHP versions.

## Experimental features

- [Experimental](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/): Overview of experimental features, whose API may change in future versions.
- [Markdown](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/markdown.html): How to convert Markdown text to HTML.
- [Storage utilities](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/storage.html): How to read, write and manage files in the application's storage directory.
- [Validation](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/validation.html): How to validate input data and routes with predefined rules.
- [CSV/TSV Reader](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/csv-tsv-reader.html): How to read CSV and TSV files with `Csv` and `Tsv`, using flags (associative columns, skipping blank lines and the header), DTOs, custom end-of-line and conversion to JSON, CSV, TSV, HTML and XML.
- [HTTP method override](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/http-features.html#http-method-override): How to simulate methods such as PUT, PATCH, DELETE and QUERY in HTML forms (which only support GET and POST) with `Method::override()`, using the `_method` parameter or the `x-http-method-override` header, with configurable methods, header and parameter.
- [Cookie Jar (HTTP)](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/http-cookies.html): How to set, read and delete cookies grouped by jar (`jar:` prefix) with `CookieJar`, including the Domain, Expires, HttpOnly, Partitioned, Path, SameSite and Secure attributes.
- [Cache (HTTP)](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/experimental/http-cache.html): How to cache dynamic responses with `Cache`, using `ETag`, `If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since` to reply with HTTP 304, with configurable lifetime, per-user isolated storage, use in routes and controllers, testing and class extension.

## Production environment features

- [OPcache](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/production/opcache.html): How to use and configure OPcache to improve performance in production.
- [Proxy & Load balancers](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/production/proxy-load-balancers.html): How to configure the application behind reverse proxies and load balancers, including `X-Forwarded-*` headers.
- [Sendfile](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/production/sendfile.html): How to use `X-Sendfile`/`X-Accel-Redirect` to delegate sending large files to the web server.

## Security

- [PHP security](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/security/): Overview of known PHP vulnerabilities affecting Inphinit applications and how to protect against them.
- [CVE-2026-115560](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/security/php-vulnerability-cve-2026-115560.html): Details of PHP vulnerability CVE-2026-115560, affected versions and mitigation measures.
- [CVE-2026-109619](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/security/php-vulnerability-cve-2026-109619.html): Details of PHP vulnerability CVE-2026-109619, affected versions and mitigation measures.
- [CVE-2026-109618](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/security/php-vulnerability-cve-2026-109618.html): Details of PHP vulnerability CVE-2026-109618, affected versions and mitigation measures.

## Packages

- [Inphinit Proxy](https://inphinit.github.io/en/docs/packages/inphinit-proxy.html): Package for forwarding requests to other servers, working as a proxy inside the application.
